before: If an attribute's legal next value depends on its current value and it meets the threshold below, it is a state machine: it belongs to a named machine definition from the first migration in which it qualifies, and a nested or parallel lifecycle is expressed in the definition, never as a loop or branch in an executor.
after: An attribute is a state machine when its legal next value depends on its current value and it meets the threshold below. Nothing else is required. before: Crossing the threshold is a design change, announced at review — never folded into a refactor.
after: Crossing the threshold is a design change, even when it arrives inside a refactor. It is announced at review, never made quietly.

before: Two lanes and one loop. The linter counts and remembers. The models read and discover. The reviewer decides.
after: Two lanes, one loop: the linter counts sentences, the models read for meaning, and the reviewer decides.
